decks.notes: This deck focuses on overwhelming the opponent with aggressive creatures while disrupting their game plan with hate cards like Trinisphere and Chancellor of the Annex. By playing efficient hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Anointed Peacekeeper, it can slow down opponents while continuing to apply pressure. The deck also includes disruptive artifacts like Chalice of the Void and Wasteland to further disrupt the opponent's strategy. Overall, the deck aims to disrupt and control the game while building a board presence to win quickly.

The deck focuses on utilizing the Paradoxical Outcome card to generate card advantage and mana acceleration by returning artifacts to hand, while also controlling the board with counterspells and removal spells. It aims to build a strong board presence and combo off to win the game quickly using the high number of artifact and mana acceleration cards. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and recursion options, enhancing the deck's overall strategy and resilience.

The deck revolves around assembling a game-winning combination of cards, usually involving Doomsday and Thassa's Oracle. It aims to set up a board state where it can win the game in one turn, using powerful card draw and manipulation spells like Ponder, Preordain, and Brainstorm. The deck also includes disruption in the form of counterspells like Force of Will and Mindbreak Trap to protect its combo. It can quickly find and assemble its combo pieces using tutors like Vampiric Tutor and Demonic Tutor, allowing for a fast and efficient win condition.

This deck focuses on efficiently drawing cards and generating mana to assemble a win condition combo, usually involving Paradoxical Outcome. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Mental Misstep to protect the combo and interact with the opponent. Utilizing fast mana sources like Black Lotus and Moxen, as well as powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Gitaxian Probe, the deck aims to quickly assemble its key pieces and either draw the entire deck or generate a game-winning board state.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on disruptive spells like Force of Will and Fatal Push to control the game, while also utilizing card advantage through spells like Treasure Cruise and Ancestral Recall. The deck aims to slow down the opponent's game plan by countering their spells and removing their threats, ultimately out-valuing them with efficient card draw and removal. Additionally, with Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion, the deck can recur valuable resources from the graveyard to maintain a steady advantage throughout the game.

This deck revolves around assembling the Doomsday combo to win the game. By using cards like Dark Ritual, Demonic Tutor, and Vampiric Tutor to quickly search for and cast Doomsday, the player can set up a winning pile of cards to be drawn with Thassa's Oracle for a game-winning victory. The deck also includes a mix of control elements like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to protect the combo and disrupt opponent's strategies. The goal is to efficiently and effectively execute the combo while managing resources and responding to opposing threats.

The deck aims to establish control over the game by using a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and disruptive permanents to disrupt the opponent's game plan. It also utilizes card advantage through cards like Dig Through Time and Lórien Revealed to ensure that it can maintain control of the game in the long run. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing for consistent recursion of low-cost permanents. Overall, the deck seeks to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent through a combination of disruption and card advantage.

This deck focuses on utilizing powerful control and disruption cards to outmaneuver opponents and dictate the pace of the game. By combining counterspells like Force of Will and Flusterstorm with powerful removal like Swords to Plowshares, the deck aims to keep the opponent's threats in check while gradually gaining card advantage through cards like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. Lurrus of the Dream-Den serves as a versatile companion that can provide additional value and resilience in longer games. Ultimately, the deck's goal is to outlast opponents and close out the game with efficient threats and disruptive spells.

The deck focuses on aggressive creatures that also disrupt the opponent's game plan, creating a challenging board state for them to navigate. By playing hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, along with disruptive artifacts like Void Mirror and Chalice of the Void, the deck aims to slow down the opponent's actions while applying pressure with creatures like Clarion Conqueror and Seasoned Dungeoneer. The mana acceleration provided by cards like Chrome Mox and Ancient Tomb allows for explosive starts, while also utilizing powerful lands like Cavern of Souls and Urza's Saga to further enhance the deck's strategy.

The key focus of this deck is to control the game through a combination of disruptive spells, removal, and card advantage. By utilizing cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Spell Pierce, the deck aims to counter or remove threats from the opponent while maintaining a card advantage with spells like Treasure Cruise and Ancestral Recall. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for recurring low-cost permanents, adding to the deck's resilience. Overall, the deck seeks to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent in a Vintage 1 vs 1 format.

The main idea of this deck is to control the game by utilizing powerful spells and efficient mana sources. By combining control elements like counterspells and card draw with powerful win conditions like Brain Freeze and Tinker, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's plans while advancing its own strategy. Gifts Ungiven is a key card that allows for flexible searching and toolbox options, while cards like Hullbreacher and Underworld Breach provide additional layers of disruption and value. Overall, the deck is built to outmaneuver and outclass opponents in a Vintage 1 vs 1 format.

The deck focuses on assembling a powerful combo using cards such as The One Ring, Coveted Jewel, and Time Vault in order to generate massive mana advantage and draw cards through Paradoxical Outcome. It utilizes artifacts like Grim Monolith, Mystic Forge, and Mana Crypt to accelerate its game plan, while also incorporating counterspells like Force of Will for protection. The deck aims to create an overwhelming board presence and advantage to outpace the opponent and secure victory quickly.

The deck focuses on utilizing Paradoxical Outcome to generate card advantage and mana ramp by bouncing back artifacts to hand. It aims to efficiently cycle through the deck with card draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Brainstorm, while using powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Mana Crypt to accelerate mana production. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares to interact with the opponent's game plan. The end goal is to assemble a combo win condition or overwhelm the opponent with a high volume of spells and threats.

This combo-focused Doomsday deck aims to quickly search for and set up a Doomsday pile, using cards like Vampiric Tutor, Dark Ritual, and Demonic Tutor to find key pieces. By utilizing powerful cantrips like Ponder and Consider, along with disruption like Flusterstorm and Force of Will, the deck aims to protect its combo and win condition. Once the Doomsday pile is set up with Thassa's Oracle, the deck can quickly win the game by drawing the necessary cards in a single turn. The deck is designed to be efficient and focused on achieving a fast and decisive victory.

The deck focuses on controlling the game by utilizing a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and card draw. It aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy while maintaining card advantage and board control. By utilizing powerful cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Ancestral Recall, the deck seeks to outvalue and outlast the opponent. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion offers additional value by allowing the player to recur important cards from the graveyard. Overall, the deck prioritizes control and consistency to secure victory.

The deck focuses on controlling the opponent's plays through a combination of counter spells, removal, and disruptive creatures like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade. It also utilizes card advantage with powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for repeated value from the graveyard. Additionally, the deck includes mana denial with cards like Wasteland and Strip Mine to disrupt the opponent's mana base. Overall, the deck aims to dominate the game through careful resource management and disruption.
